topic: spain train collision death toll rises
headline_marked: [[68 killed]] in Spain train crash, 80 injured as one train hits stationary one
headline: 68 killed in Spain train crash, 80 injured as one train hits stationary one
summary: A high-speed train collided with a stationary train in Spain, killing 68 people and injuring 80. The crash is the deadliest rail accident in Europe since 2013.
details: A collision between a high-speed train and a stationary train in Spain has resulted in 68 fatalities and 80 injuries. Among the injured, 15 are in critical condition. Rescue workers are continuing to search the mangled carriages for more bodies. This marks the second fatal rail accident in Spain this year and the deadliest in Europe since 2013.

The accident occurred around 9 AM local time on Wednesday in a rural area of Spain's Castilla-La Mancha region. Several carriages of one train derailed and fell down an embankment following the impact. Emergency services, including ambulances, rescue helicopters, and body transport vehicles, were dispatched to the scene immediately.

Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez expressed the nation's grief, stating that the entire country mourns. Speaking from near the crash site south of Madrid, he pledged a full investigation into the tragic event and vowed to address any shortcomings or failures identified. He noted that the two rail accidents this year appear unrelated.

Sánchez emphasized the need to strengthen safety measures to restore public confidence in the country's high-speed rail system, deeming two high-speed train accidents in the same year unacceptable for a country like Spain.

Spain's Transport Minister Óscar Puente revealed that the Renfe-operated train was given a red signal because a train ahead was stationary. However, the train was allowed to proceed despite the active signal.

Puente explained to reporters in Madrid that the red signal was issued due to a fault in the computerised signaling system, which automatically halted train traffic. The decision to restart the Renfe train was a mistake.

Renfe, the train operating company, stated in a release that its train collided with the Iryo-operated train ahead after receiving permission to move. However, Renfe was unaware of why the Iryo train was stopped. The exact sequence of events, the rail traffic conditions at the time, and the cause of the collision are to be determined through an investigation.
Iryo confirmed that it has taken emergency measures following the accident. However, the state railway infrastructure manager Adif and Iryo did not immediately respond to requests for comment.

Rescue workers conducted searches within the damaged carriages for trapped passengers. Emiliano García-Page, the regional government chief of Castilla-La Mancha, confirmed the death toll reached 68. Searches continued after dark, with uncertainty about whether more bodies would be found after the damaged carriages are removed.

Injured passengers, some with bloodstains and bandages, were moved to a nearby road. Spain's Health Minister Mónica García reported that 15 of the 80 injured individuals are in extremely serious condition.

Passenger Salvador Ariza, 62, recounted the horrific experience, stating he was able to escape as he was near the door. Other passengers were breaking windows to get out, with many trapped between seats. He estimated at least eight deaths in his carriage alone.

Another passenger, Rafael Barceló, survived because he had gotten up to get coffee. He described a sudden, powerful impact that threw passengers around. He believes at least eight people died in his carriage.

A school was set up for relatives of missing passengers to wait for news. Ana, a relative at the school in Úrda, reported that her husband Pepe had not yet been located. While his name was not on the list of identified victims, rescuers found their pet dog, Tressy.
Renfe has launched a special hotline to assist families of the deceased and missing. The company has also suspended ticket sales for the Madrid-Andalusia high-speed rail line until December 13.

topic: bus-car crash kills mother-daughter in Chakaria
headline_marked: Mother and daughter [[killed in head-on collision]] in Chakaria
headline: Mother and daughter killed in head-on collision in Chakaria
summary: A passenger bus and a private car crashed on the Chittagong-Cox's Bazar highway, leaving two family members dead and two others injured.
details: A head-on collision between a passenger bus and a private car on the Chittagong-Cox's Bazar highway in Chakaria, Cox's Bazar, has left a mother and her 10-year-old daughter dead.
The accident occurred around 3:30 PM on Wednesday, October 28, at a bend in the road near the Amtala hill in the Baniarchara area of the colony.
The deceased have been identified as Ismat Ara (55) and her daughter Aisha (10), both residents of the Halishahar area of Chittagong.
Two others were injured in the crash: the private car driver, Ashikur Rahman (27), and Ismat Ara's son, Samrat (30).

According to Jakibul Islam, In-charge of the Chiringa Highway Police Station, the Shadhin Travels bus was traveling from Chittagong to Cox's Bazar when it collided head-on with the oncoming private car.
Police have seized both the bus and the private car. The bodies of the victims have been recovered and kept at the the Chakaria Upazila Health Complex.
Following the request of the family members, the police are processing the handover of the bodies without an autopsy.

According to Jakibul Islam, In-charge of the Chiringa Highway Police Station, the Shadhin Travels bus was traveling from Chittagong to Cox's Bazar when it collided head-on with the oncoming private car.
